note: A subscript is an expression, not a bare name. `array_subscript_2d` pins the comma rule -- that `Recipe[Row,Col]` is one operand and not two. This pins what is INSIDE the brackets: `Recipe_Buffer[Current_Step.Index]` reads the pointer, not the pointer and a phantom member. The first implementation swept identifiers out of the brackets, so it read both `Current_Step` and `Index`; `Index` is a real and unrelated controller tag here, so the sweep emitted a FALSE read edge. Same defect as expression_member_path, one level down and in a different function (`split_operand` rather than the expression walk), which is why it gets its own fixture -- fixing one did not fix the other. The index read is genuine and stays: the controller does read Current_Step to compute the address.
